name: The Devil Went Down to Georgia

info.album: The Devil Went Down to Georgia (America's 250th)

podcast.body: This song was featured in the "Urban Cowboy" movie, playing in the background during a scene where Wes prepares to ride the bull before attempting to rob Gilley's nightclub. "the double went down to Georgia by Charlie Daniels was playing in the background. Perfect."

This song, from the 1979 album "Million Mile Reflections," was originally intended as instrumental filler with no lyrics, to provide fiddle music to fill gaps on the album. Lyrics were later added, developing a "sell your soul narrative" about a character named Johnny. It was inspired by Stephen Vincent Benét's poem "The Mountain Whippoorwill." Charlie Daniels considered the fiddle a bridge from rock to the band's bluegrass roots. The song became a huge crossover hit, reaching number three on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1979, and was prominently featured in the 1980 movie "Urban Cowboy," introducing its "bad-ass fiddle playing" to new audiences and regions. The Charlie Daniels Band performed it on Austin City Limits in 1981. "The devil went down to Georgia made it to number three on the billboard hot 100 in 1979. Yes, it was a huge crossover hit."
